headline: Red Sox bats go silent while rookie minicamp brings energy to Foxborough
morning_brew: Mother's Day at Fenway was another tough watch as the bats went quiet in a four to one loss to the Rays. Payton Tolle put together five innings of work on an emotional day, but giving up seven hits and three runs was too much for an offense that could only muster one run on eight hits. Mickey Gasper was the lone bright spot with three hits, but it is absolutely brutal when your top of the order goes combined zero for eight. We are sitting at seventeen and twenty-three now, looking at the Phillies coming to town next.

Down in Foxborough, the news is a bit more optimistic as the young kids are getting their feet wet at rookie minicamp. Behren Morton is already making some noise, and people are starting to wonder if Eli Raridon has that untapped potential we heard about during the draft. Protecting the future is the name of the game, and seeing these guys get to work is a nice distraction from the mess at Fenway. It is early, but building that chemistry between the quarterback and his new targets is exactly what this offense needs.

The winter teams are in different spots right now, with the C's looking at mock drafts and the B's still grinding in the postseason. Seeing the lottery results come in is a reminder of how much work the front office has to do to get back to the mountaintop after that early exit on Causeway Street. Eighteen banners is a lot of history to live up to, and this fan base does not have much patience for retooling years. Front office better be on the phone right now to find that missing piece while we wait to see if the Bruins can make a deep run.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox's Payton Tolle honors his mom, who died two years ago
news_digest.dans_take: A deeply moving tribute on a difficult day, respect to the kid for gutting it out on the mound.

news_digest.dans_take: Drake Maye is going to need every weapon available if this rebuild is going to work.
